diagnostic_evidence.quote: cases there exists a constant $C>0$, independent of $h$, such that \[ \lVert\mathbf v_h\rVert \le C\lVert\nabla \mathbf v_h\rVert,\qquad \lVert\mathbf C_h\rVert \le C\lVert\nabla \mathbf C_h\rVert \] for all $\mathbf v_{h}\in \mathcal{V}_{h}$ and $\mathbf C_{h}\in \mathcal{C}_{h}$.
In the periodic case, the corresponding estimate is used on the subspace of periodic functions with zero spatial mean.
In the periodic case, we take $\mathcal{V}=H^{1}_{\mathrm{per}}\left(\Omega\right)^{2}$, $\mathcal{C}=H^{1}_{\mathrm{per}}\left(\Omega\right)^{2}$
In the periodic case, we additionally assume that the velocity and magnetic field have zero spatial mean.

issues.failure_explanation: In the periodic case the discrete spaces are subspaces of the full periodic space H^1_per and contain nonzero constant fields, for which ||v_h|| <= C||grad v_h|| is false; the inequality holds only on the zero-mean subspace, as the paper itself states one sentence earlier. The stability proof's force estimate above (and the convergence proof's nonlinear estimates) applies the inequality to discrete solutions that are never shown to have zero spatial mean; moreover the scheme does not conserve the mean exactly, since testing the discrete momentum equation with a constant c gives Delta_tau^alpha(mean of u_h^n) = mean of f^n + (1/2) mean of (div u_h) u_h - (1/2) mean of (div B_h) B_h. Hence the claimed universal inequality is false as stated and both proofs have a gap in the periodic case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the periodic case take V_h and C_h to be zero-mean subspaces of H^1_per(Omega)^2 and assume zero-mean initial data and forces; then the discrete solutions have zero mean, the Poincare inequality applies as claimed, and both proofs go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: In the periodic case the stability estimate of thm:stability and the convergence estimate of thm:convergence are not established as written, because the Poincare inequality is applied outside its valid scope; the Dirichlet-case results are unaffected.
issues.title: Periodic Poincare inequality claimed for all discrete functions though it holds only on the zero-mean subspace
issues.why_classification: The defect is removed by a short local condition (zero-mean discrete subspace and data) with no change to the method, conclusion, rate, or scope, so the issue is minor.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting the fully discrete equations (20)-(22) from the semidiscrete equations (15)-(17) and testing with (xi_u^n, xi_p^n, xi_B^n) produces, in the momentum equation, the pressure term -(p^n - p_h^n, div xi_u^n) = -(psi_p^n + xi_p^n, div xi_u^n) and the diffusion cross terms (1/Re)(grad psi_u^n, grad xi_u^n) and (1/Rm)(grad psi_B^n, grad xi_B^n). None of these terms appear in the displayed error equation (28), so the displayed identity is false as written. The subsequent estimates never bound the pressure terms (xi_p^n is chosen as a test function but never used, and subtracting the continuity equations gives only 0 = 0, so the pressure is not eliminated), and Assumption (11) assumes no regularity on the pressure p. Controlling the pressure contribution requires the standard Stokes inf-sup pressure-error estimate ||p^n - p_h^n|| <= C(||grad(u^n - u_h^n)|| + inf_{q_h} ||p^n - q_h||) together with a pressure regularity hypothesis, which the paper neither states nor proves; the diffusion cross terms are only absorbed after being added to the equation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing pressure terms -(psi_p^n + xi_p^n, div xi_u^n) and the diffusion cross terms (1/Re)(grad psi_u^n, grad xi_u^n) + (1/Rm)(grad psi_B^n, grad xi_B^n) to the error equation; bound the pressure contribution via the standard Stokes inf-sup pressure-error estimate ||p^n - p_h^n|| <= C(||grad(u^n-u_h^n)|| + inf_{q_h}||p^n - q_h||) after adding a pressure regularity assumption (e.g. p in L^infty(0,T;H^{l+1}(Omega)), obtainable from the momentum equation and the assumed W^{1,infty} regularity of u and B) to Assumption (11); absorb all resulting terms by Young's inequality as is done for the other terms. The diffusion cross terms are absorbed directly. The conclusion and rate survive.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence estimate of thm:convergence does not follow from the proof as written: the error equation is incomplete and the pressure error is never controlled, so the stated O(h^{min{l,m}} + tau) bound is formally unsupported. Numerical results citing the theorem are not thereby invalidated, but they are formally unbacked.
issues.title: Error equation in the convergence proof omits the pressure terms and the diffusion projection cross terms
issues.why_classification: The gap is closed by a contained but nontrivial new argument (the Stokes inf-sup pressure-error estimate) plus an extra regularity hypothesis; the proof architecture, conclusion, and rate survive, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.failure_explanation: The convergence proof bounds the L1 truncation remainders by ||r_1^n||^2 + ||r_2^n||^2 <= C tau^2 (the tau^2 term in I_2). The classical L1 error estimate behind this, ({}^C D_t^{nu(t_n)} phi)(t_n) = Delta_tau^{nu(t_n)} phi^n + O(tau), requires phi' to be Lipschitz in time (equivalently partial_t^2 phi in L^infty), which yields the standard O(tau^{2-nu}) bound. Assumption (11) only assumes partial_t u, partial_t B in L^infty (plus spatial regularity), under which the L1 error need not be O(tau). Hence the estimate I_2 <= C(... + tau^2), and with it the claimed first-order temporal rate, relies on a regularity premise the paper never assumes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Assumption (11) that partial_t^2 u, partial_t^2 B in L^infty(0,T;L^2(Omega)^2) (or that partial_t u, partial_t B are Lipschitz in time), which yields the classical L1 remainder bound O(tau^{2-nu}) subset O(tau) and hence ||r_i^n|| <= C tau. No other change is needed; the method, rate, and scope are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The temporal O(tau) rate in thm:convergence is unproven under the stated assumptions; the proof needs an additional standard time-regularity condition on the exact solution.
issues.title: O(tau) bound on the variable-order L1 truncation remainder used in the convergence proof is not justified by the stated regularity
issues.why_classification: The gap is repaired by adding one standard local regularity condition to the existing assumption, with the method, conclusion, rate, and advertised scope all surviving, so the issue is minor.
